part_title: EC2 Fundamentals and AI Accelerator Choices

scenes.title: Amazon EC2
scenes.narration: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud, or E C two, provides virtual machine instances on AWS. A basic web application can run its code on an EC2 instance, but the overall architecture often includes more than the instance itself. Elastic Block Store provides attached block storage, a load balancer distributes incoming requests, and an Auto Scaling group can adjust the number of running instances based on configured demand or policies. Those are separate services with different roles. If two instances serve requests behind a load balancer, the balancer does not itself create replacement machines; Auto Scaling manages fleet capacity. The student should identify the difference between compute capacity, persistent storage, traffic distribution and automatic instance count. In a managed AI services course, EC2 is a general-purpose building block rather than a dedicated language-processing API.

scenes.title: EC2 sizing & configuration options
scenes.narration: Sizing EC2 starts with the workload's operating system, processor architecture, CPU, memory and storage needs. An Amazon Machine Image defines a starting system image; the chosen instance type provides compute resources. Amazon EBS offers attached block volumes, Amazon EFS offers a shared file system and instance store provides host-local temporary storage. The right choice depends on data persistence and access patterns. Networking and security also matter: security groups filter permitted traffic, and IAM roles let applications receive AWS permissions without embedding permanent credentials. User data can automate setup during instance launch, but it should not contain passwords or long-lived secrets. A helpful exam scenario asks whether the application needs a mounted operating-system volume, a shared file system or short-lived scratch space. Choose each service for its specific responsibility.

scenes.title: AWS hardware choices for AI workloads
scenes.narration: AI and machine learning workloads can benefit from specialized accelerators, but the best hardware depends on supported software and measured performance. GPU-based EC2 instances are often used with compatible training and inference frameworks. AWS Trainium is designed for supported model-training workloads, while AWS Inferentia focuses on supported inference. AWS Neuron provides tooling for supported accelerator environments. Before choosing a family, check that the particular model, framework, numerical precision and deployment stack are compatible. Compare observed throughput, latency, total cost and operational complexity rather than assuming the newest chip always wins. Claims about energy use or price performance depend on generation and benchmark; measure your own workload. A beginner should distinguish training, which updates model parameters, from inference, which uses a trained model to make predictions or generate outputs.
